phrases.text: So
welcome back again.
Time for one more problem.
Now in this problem,
a tourist
travels one hundred twenty kilometer
at
forty kilometer per hour.
Then the next one hundred twenty kilometer
is traveled at sixty kilometer per hour.
The question is asking us to find the average speed for the total two hundred forty kilometer trip.
Now be careful here,
we should not directly average forty and sixty.
We should not say forty plus sixty divided by two is fifty.
Why?
Because average speed depends on total distance and total time.
So first,
we need to find the time taken in both parts.
Now we know the formula.
Time is equal to distance divided by speed.
For the first one hundred twenty kilometer, speed is forty, so time is one hundred twenty divided by forty.
That gives us three hours.
For the second one hundred twenty kilometer, speed is sixty, so time is one hundred twenty divided by sixty.
That gives us two hours.
Now total distance is one hundred twenty plus one hundred twenty,
which is two hundred forty kilometer.
Total time is three plus two, which is five hours. Now average speed is equal to total distance divided by total time.
So average speed is two hundred forty divided by five.
That gives us forty-eight kilometers per hour.
So the final answer will be forty-eight kilometers per hour.
Hence,
option C, forty-eight kilometers per hour is correct.
